EngLawHistories: 1.Promulgated by Presidential Order No. Hua-Zong-I-Yi-Zi-11500041151 on May 8, 2026, with a total of 94 Articles. The date of enforcement shall be prescribed by the Executive Yuan by order.

EngLawArticles.EngArticleContent: Chapter I. General Provisions

The following Act is hereby established to promote the sound physical and mental development of, and gender equality among, children; safeguard the right of children to receive care and education appropriate to their age and developmental needs; ensure the quality of childcare services; enhance public childcare capacity; support nationalsin balancing childcare and employment responsibilities; and establish a comprehensive childcare service system.
Matters related to the rights and interests of children not provided herein shall be governed by the applicable provisions of the Child and Juvenile Welfare and Rights Protection Act.

The term “competent authority” as used herein refers to the Ministry of Health and Welfare at the central government level, the municipal government at the special municipality level, and the county (city) government at the county (city) level.
For any provisions set forth herein involving the functions and responsibilities of the competent authority for a relevant enterprise, such authority shall be required to cooperate.

Definition of terms:
1. “Child”: A person under 12 years of age
2. “Childcare services”: Care and education services appropriate to a child’s age and developmental needs provided by family childcare personnel or childcare institutions
3. “Family childcare”: Paid childcare services provided in a family environment for a child under 12 years of age by a person other than a relative within the third degree of kinship, either at the caregiver’s residence or at the child’s residence
4. “Childcare service in the provider’s home”: Childcare services provided by family childcare personnel at a registered service location upon the entrustment of the child’s legal representative or actual guardian.
5. “Childcare service in the child’s home”: Childcare services provided by family childcare personnel at the child’s residence or another designated residence upon the entrustment of the child’s legal representative or actual guardian.
6. “Fixed-site temporary childcare”: Non-regularly scheduled childcare services provided, either directly or through entrustment to a nonprofit legal entity, institution, or organization, by the competent authority of a special municipality, county, or city (collectively, “local authority”) at a designated location that meets the environmental requirements for child safety
7. “Childcare institution”: A public nursery, nursery service center, or cooperative childcare institution that provides childcare services for children under two years of age
8. “Public nursery”: An institution providing childcare services for up to 12 children under two years of age, operated either directly or through entrustment to a nonprofit legal entity, institution, or organization, by the local authority
9. “Nursery service center”: An institution established by a government agency (institution), school, legal entity, organization, hospital, business, or natural person to provide childcare services for children under two years of age
10. “Cooperative childcare institution”: An institution established to provide childcare services for children under two years of age in consideration of the special circumstances of offshore islands, remote areas, or Indigenous communities, or to meet the childcare needs of the lineal blood descendants of employees at government agencies (institutions), state-owned enterprises, companies, schools, or nongovernmental organizations (NGOs)
11. “Family childcare personnel”: A person who holds a family childcare service certificate issued by the local authority
12. “Persons residing with family childcare personnel”: The spouse or a lineal blood relative, collateral blood relative, cohabitant of, or other person residing with, family childcare personnel
13. “Family childcare service center”: A nonprofit legal entity, institution, or organization entrusted by the local authority to handle matters relating to the registration, administration, case matching, supervision, oversight, inspection, and dispute resolution of family childcare services
14. “Responsible person”: The person under whose name a childcare institution is registered in accordance with this Act and other applicable regulations
15. “Supervisory personnel”: Personnel responsible for the overall administration of a childcare institution
16. “Institutional childcare personnel”: Personnel who provide care and education services in a childcare institution
17. “Childcare professionals”: A collective term for family childcare personnel, supervisory personnel, and institutional childcare personnel
18. “Staff members”: A collective term for personnel working in a childcare institution other than the responsible person, supervisory personnel, and institutional childcare personnel
19. “Childcare-related personnel”: A collective term for responsible persons, childcare professionals, and staff members
20. “Care dispute”: A dispute arising from a legal representative’s or actual guardian’s belief that the quality of childcare services is below reasonable expectations in such a manner as can be attributed to childcare-related personnel

The implementation of childcare service policies shall be coordinated in close collaboration with families and communities in order to achieve the following objectives:
1. To satisfy children’s physical care needs
2. To create an appropriate and safe environment conducive to children’s growth and development
3. To foster positive attachment relationships between children and caregivers
4. To create a learning environment that promotes equality, democratic values, and respect for differences
5. To enrich children’s opportunities for play, exploration, and experiential learning
6. To encourage teamwork and help children develop peer relationships
7. To inspire children to care for others and for the environment
8. To encourage children’s expression and participation
9. To support families with children by building collaborative partnerships

Childcare services shall be administered with children’s best interest as the primary consideration, and quality childcare services shall be provided through accessible, affordable, and readily available means.
Government agencies, childcare institutions, childcare-related personnel, and families shall work together to advance and promote the comprehensive development of childcare services.
The government shall provide priority access to the appropriate childcare services for children on offshore islands, in remote areas, and from Indigenous communities, as well as children in need of assistance due to financial, physical, cognitive, cultural, or ethnic factors (hereinafter, “children requiring assistance”).

The responsibilities of the central competent authority shall be as follows:
1. Planning, formulation, promotion, and study of nationwide childcare policies, regulations, and programs
2. Supervision, coordination, and oversight of childcare services implemented by local authorities
3. Allocation of central government budgets and subsidies for childcare services
4. Planning of childcare service-related supervision, recognition, subsidization, and evaluation
5. Planning and implementation of childcare service-related professional training
6. Collection, survey, tabulation, and disclosure of nationwide childcare service statistics
7. Regular surveys of childcare service needs and release of statistical and analytical data as a basis for childcare service policy formulation
8. Assistance in the establishment of childcare personnel organizations and parental associations
9. Other matters related to childcare services at the national level
The “childcare service statistics” described in Subparagraph 6 of the preceding paragraph shall include, at minimum, family childcare service providers’ and childcare institutions’ fee schedules (service items and service fees), evaluation results, penalties received, and other related matters.

The responsibilities of local authorities shall be as follows:
1. Planning, formulation, promotion, study, and implementation of local childcare policies and programs
2. Implementation of childcare policies, regulations, and programs formulated by the central competent authority
3. Organization of childcare service-related professional training
4. Supervision, oversight, and inspection of local family childcare service centers
5. Matters related to the registration, management, case matching, supervision, oversight, and inspection of local family childcare service providers
6. Matters related to the establishment, management, supervision, oversight, inspection, and evaluation of local childcare institutions
7. Collection, survey, tabulation, and disclosure of local childcare service statistics
8. Assistance in the establishment of childcare personnel and parental associations
9. Setting of standards for administrative fines in the event of violations of this Act
10. Other matters related to the strategic planning and oversight of local childcare services
The “childcare service statistics” described in Subparagraph 7 of the preceding paragraph shall include, at minimum, fee schedules (service items and service fees), evaluation results, punitive decisions, and other matters pertaining to family childcare service providers and childcare institutions under the local authority’s jurisdiction.

The central competent authority shall establish a childcare advisory committee to systematically plan, coordinate, advise on, and promote childcare services; develop a family childcare workforce; set standards for fees, refunds, and fee adjustments for family childcare service providers (and fees and refunds for childcare institutions); and handle other childcare service-related matters.
Each local authority shall establish a childcare review committee to systematically plan, coordinate, and advise on childcare services under its jurisdiction and to review the fee/refund standards and fee adjustment principles set forth by the central competent authority under the preceding paragraph.
Members of the childcare advisory committee described in Paragraph 1 and of the childcare review committee described in the preceding paragraph shall include representatives from the competent social welfare authority, competent health authority, and competent labor authority; scholars and experts in a related field; family childcare service personnel or representatives from their associations; childcare institution association representatives; child welfare organization representatives; parent representatives, women’s rights group representatives; and labor rights group representatives.
When handling matters involving Indigenous Peoples or persons with disabilities, the childcare advisory committee described in Paragraph 1 and childcare review committee described in Paragraph 2 shall additionally include members of the corresponding community during deliberations.
Experts, scholars, and civic association representatives, as described in the preceding paragraph, must constitute at least half of the membership body and may not concurrently be a legislator or local council representative. Members of any gender shall constitute at least one third of the membership body.
A childcare institution’s responsible person may not serve as a committee member under Paragraph 3 as anything other than a childcare institution representative. In the event of a change in affiliation of any members described under Paragraph 3, the competent authority shall re-appoint such members accordingly.

Childcare services shall be child-centered and shall, while giving equal weight to gender, ethnic, and cultural equality, encompass care and education appropriate to children’s age and developmental needs grounded in respect for children’s development. The scope of such services shall be as follows:
1. Providing a clean, hygienic, safe, and developmentally appropriate environment for children
2. Providing children with adequate nutrition, healthcare, daily living care, learning and play activities, and services related to their social development
3. Documenting children’s daily living, growth, and referral records
4. Providing childcare consultation and information related to family support
5. Other services beneficial to children’s development
The implementation standards for the scope of childcare services described in the preceding paragraph shall be determined by the central competent authority.

The government may provide subsidies for children receiving childcare services based on the financial situation of a child’s family or other special circumstances. The regulations governing the eligibility, conditions, amounts, definition of special circumstances, and other related matters for such subsidies shall be determined by the central competent authority.
The legal representative or actual guardian of a child may open a dedicated account with a financial institution and, after specifying the name and address of the financial institution, account number, and beneficiary name and obtaining approval from the local authority, use such account exclusively for the deposit of the subsidies described in the preceding paragraph.
The subsidies provided under the preceding paragraph and deposits in dedicated accounts shall not be subject to seizure, assignment, set-off, provision of security, or compulsory enforcement.

The central competent authority shall formulate policies for the development and promotion of family childcare and conduct regular reviews to strengthen family childcare workforce and improve the quality of care.
Local authorities shall commend childcare service providers with outstanding performance.
Chapter II. Family childcare

A person who meets the qualifications for childcare professionals described in Article 45 shall complete an application form and submit the relevant supporting documents and information to the local authority for registration. Such person may provide family childcare services only after obtaining a family childcare service certificate.
Family childcare personnel must apply to the competent authority for approval before suspending services during the service period.
The local authority may, either directly or by commissioning a family childcare service center to do so, handle the registration, administration, case matching, supervision, oversight, and inspection of family childcare personnel. Such inspections may be conducted without prior notice.
No person may evade, obstruct, or refuse oversight or inspection of family childcare personnel conducted by the local authority or a family childcare service center. During an inspection, no person may conceal any child under any excuse.
Regulations governing the registration, number of children allowed, supervision, administration, inspection, revocation of registration, and other matters governing family childcare personnel under Paragraph 1 shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

Family childcare personnel who provide childcare services in their own home shall prominently display their family childcare service certificate in a clearly visible place at their registered service location.

Service fees and refundable items for family childcare services, and the principles for setting and adjusting fees, shall be announced by the central competent authority.
The central competent authority shall regularly convene with local authorities, scholars and experts, and civic association representatives to review and update the principles for adjusting service fees and refunds for family childcare services, with consideration given to the national and local consumer price indices, household disposable income, the working conditions of childcare personnel, and other relevant factors.
The local authority shall, in accordance with the fee and refund items and principles for adjusting such fees and refunds published under Paragraph 1, set and publish the local fee and refund standards for childcare services in each district based on the types of childcare services and fee assessment circumstances within its jurisdiction.
The fee and refund standards for childcare services described in the preceding paragraph shall be reviewed at least once every two years.

Family childcare personnel are prohibited from collecting any fees other than those specified in the fee and refund standards published by the local authority under Paragraph 3 of the preceding article.

Before initiating childcare services, family childcare personnel shall enter into a written contract setting out the relevant childcare rights and obligations with the legal representative or actual guardian of the child placed in their charge. A copy of the contract shall be supplied to the local family childcare service center.
The format and contents of the written contract described in the preceding paragraph shall be standardized by the central competent authority in a standard contract form that stipulates the compulsory and prohibited terms.

Family childcare personnel shall ensure that they are covered by professional liability insurance before the date on which a child is admitted to their care.
In the event of an insured incident during the coverage period described in the preceding paragraph, the competent family childcare service center shall proactively assist in the insurance claims process.

During the service period, family childcare personnel shall devote themselves to their childcare responsibilities at the designated service location and shall not engage in any of the following:
1. Concurrently holding another job, running a business, or engaging in activities that could negatively affect the quality of care during service hours
2. Leaving a child under six years of age, or a child requiring special care, alone or in the charge of an unsuitable person
3. Other conduct that could potentially impact the quality of care and thereby jeopardize the safety of a child in care
If family childcare personnel must leave the service location described in the preceding paragraph due to an emergency, they shall, prior to leaving, notify the competent family childcare service center and the child’s legal representative or actual guardian and arrange for other family childcare personnel or appropriate personnel to provide temporary care for the child.

The local authority shall formulate emergency care procedures for acute illness and accidental injury occurring during the course of family childcare services.
Should a child experience acute illness or accidental injury, family childcare personnel shall, in accordance with the principles described in the preceding paragraph, carry out the required emergency care procedures, escort the child to the designated medical institution, and call the emergency medical services hotline for assistance. Family childcare personnel must also take all necessary measures until the legal representative or actual guardian arrives.
Family childcare service centers shall provide guidance to family childcare personnel to ensure the implementation of the procedures described in Paragraph 1.

Should the legal representative or actual guardian of a child be concerned with the manner or scope of childcare services provided by family childcare personnel, they may request an explanation from the family childcare personnel and may, through mutual agreement, modify or adjust such services as necessary.

During fixed-site temporary childcare services, the service location shall meet the environmental safety requirements for family childcare, and the personnel shall possess the qualifications required for family childcare personnel.
Matters governing the oversight, inspection, and supervision of and other applicable regulations pertaining to fixed-site temporary childcare services, as described in the preceding paragraph, shall be formulated by the central competent authority.

The responsibilities of family childcare service centers shall be as follows:
1. Recruiting, reserving, supporting, facilitating exchanges among, providing in-service training for, supervising, overseeing, managing, and auditing family childcare personnel
2. Processing applications for, changes to, and reissuance of family childcare service certificates.
3. Processing reports of changes in childcare arrangements submitted by family childcare personnel
4. Matching and referring childcare service cases, and assisting in the execution of written childcare contracts
5. Mediating disputes arising under Article 67, Paragraph 1herein
6. Providing childcare consultation and promoting childcare services to parents and community members
7. Other matters related to family childcare services assigned or entrusted by the central competent authority or the local authority.
Regulations related to the principles for performing the duties described in the preceding paragraph shall be formulated by the central competent authority.

Local authorities shall be responsible for overseeing and conducting inspections at family childcare service centers and may entrust professional institutions or organizations to provide supervision.
Family childcare service centers may not evade, obstruct, or refuse the oversight, inspection, or supervision described in the preceding paragraph.
Matters governing the oversight, inspection, and supervision described in the preceding two paragraphs, as well as other applicable regulations, shall be formulated by the central competent authority.

Before a local authority hires family childcare personnel in accordance with the law to provide care and placement for children, it shall first assess the suitability of the personnel, ensure that such personnel have completed the necessary professional training related to child placement, and establish a visitation mechanism for the placement period.
Matters governing assessment criteria, training courses and hours, and visitation frequency described in the preceding paragraph, as well other applicable regulations, shall be formulated by the central competent authority.
Chapter III. Childcare institutions

Nursery service centers may be established by special municipality governments, county (city) governments, township governments, mountain Indigenous districts of a special municipality, schools, legal entities, civic associations, hospitals, businesses, or natural persons.
To establish a nursery service center, an application shall be submitted to the local authority together with the relevant supporting documents and information. Childcare services may be provided only after a permit is issued.
A nursery service center established by a government agency (institution) pursuant to Article 23, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 2 of the Gender Equality in Employment Act shall admit children in the following order of priority:
1. Lineal blood descendants of employees
2. Children requiring assistance
3. Children of employees of the nursery service center
4. Children other than those specified in the preceding three subparagraphs
A nursery service center established by a school, legal entity, hospital, or business pursuant to Article 23, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 2 of the Gender Equality in Employment Act shall primarily admit lineal blood descendants of its employees and of those employees with whom it has entered into a contract for joint childcare services. Should remaining childcare places be available, the nursery service center may then admit other children, pending approval from the local authority.

The local authority shall establish, or commission the establishment and operation of, public nurseries and nursery service centers and shall prescribe a certain percentage of priority admission places for children requiring assistance.
A nonprofit legal entity, institution, or organization may, after participating in a selection process pursuant to an announcement by the local authority, be commissioned to establish and operate a public nursery or nursery service center.
Following commissioning under the preceding paragraph, the nonprofit legal entity, institution, or organization shall submit supporting documents and information to the local authority to apply for permission to establish a public nursery or nursery service center. Childcare services may be provided only after a permit is issued.
Matters governing the requirements and procedures for establishment permits; revocation of permission; expansion, relocation, suspension, termination, and resumption of business; floor area requirements; facilities and equipment; allocation of childcare-related personnel, ratio of childcare personnel to children admitted for care, and number of children admitted for care; and other regulations applicable to nursery service centers and public nurseries shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

Offshore islands and remote areas may establish community cooperative childcare institutions to address geographical limitations and children’s daily living and care needs.
To foster an environment for Indigenous children that is conducive to learning Indigenous languages and cultures, and in keeping with Indigenous traditions of communal care, Indigenous cooperative childcare institutions may be established in Indigenous communities. The central competent authority or the competent authority for Indigenous Peoples may provide subsidies for the establishment and operation of such institutions.
Government agencies (institutions), schools, state-owned enterprises, companies, and nongovernmental organizations may establish workplace cooperative childcare institutions at their respective locations to care for the lineal blood descendants of their employees.
Childcare institutions described in Paragraph 1 or 2 may, with the permission of the local authority, be established to provide services for children under six years of age at the same location as a community or Indigenous cooperative educare service center established under the Early Childhood Education and Care Act. Matters related to the shared use of care locations shall be prescribed in accordance with Paragraph 6.
Entities and persons wishing to establish a cooperative childcare institution under Paragraphs 1 through 3 shall submit the required supporting documents and information to the local authority to apply for a permit. Childcare services may be provided only after a permit is issued.
Matters governing the geographic scope; operating methods; eligibility for admission; requirements and procedures for establishment permits; revocation of permission; expansion, relocation, suspension, termination, and resumption of business; floor area and facilities/equipment; qualifications and allocation of childcare-related personnel, ratio of childcare personnel to children admitted for care, and number of children admitted for care; and other regulations applicable to cooperative childcare institutions established under Paragraphs 1 to 4 shall be prescribed by the central competent authority in consultation with the competent authority for Indigenous Peoples, the competent labor authority, and the competent education authority.

When a child admitted by a childcare institution reaches two years of age but has not been enrolled in an educare service institution, the childcare institution may continue to care for the child until the day before the child reaches three years of age.

If a childcare institution operates at a teaching venue of a school at any level, the venue may continue to be subject to its original building use and shall be exempt from having to undergo a change of building usage permit under Article 73, Paragraph 2 of the Building Act.

Where a government agency (institution) or public school commissions a nonprofit legal entity to operate a childcare institution in keeping with national policy, and the use of public real property managed by the agency (institution) or school is necessary, such public real property shall be provided for use by the commissioned nonprofit legal entity free of charge.
If the public real property described in the preceding paragraph is not under the management of the agency (institution) or school, it may be appropriated for use or, with the approval of the managing agency, provided without charge to the agency (institution) or school.

Where a legal entity, professional institution, organization, or childcare professional operates a community or Indigenous cooperative childcare institution on an offshore island, at a remote location, or in an Indigenous community in keeping with national policy, and the use of public real property is necessary, the competent public property management agency may provide such property for use by lease. The annual rent shall be calculated based on the land value tax and house tax payable for the current period for the real property in accordance with law.
Childcare institutions shall prominently display their establishment permit in a clearly visible location on their premises.

The local authority shall be responsible for the management, oversight, and inspection of childcare institutions.
The local authority may, either directly or by appointing a professional institution or organization to do so, provide supervision to and conduct evaluations of childcare institutions. Evaluation reports and results shall be published on the local authority’s website.
The local authority shall strengthen the management, oversight, and inspection described in the preceding paragraph for childcare institutions under any of the following circumstances:
1. The childcare institution is permitted to be established at the same address as a previous childcare institution whose permit has been revoked or rescinded by the competent authority or that suspended operations of its own accord within the most recent five-year period.
2. The spouse, a blood relative within the third degree of kinship, or a relative by marriage within the third degree of kinship of the responsible person of the institution is involved in any of the circumstances described in Article 47, Paragraph 1 or Articles 49 through 51.
Childcare institutions may not evade, obstruct, or refuse the management, oversight, inspection, supervision, or evaluation described in Paragraphs 1 and 2. During an inspection, no person may conceal any child under any pretext.
Matters governing categories, items, indicators, implementation methods, publication of results, requests for review, appeals, follow-up counseling, re-evaluations, and other matters related to the evaluations described in Paragraph 2 shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

A standard for childcare institution service fees, usages, and refundable items shall be published by the central competent authority.
Private childcare institutions may, in consideration of their operating costs, set a service fee and refund schedule in accordance with the standard published by the central competent authority under the preceding paragraph. Such institutions may collect fees from and issue refunds to the legal representative or actual guardian of the child in their care only after the schedule has been reported to and approved by the local authority. The same shall apply when adjustments to the fee and refund schedule are necessary.
Childcare institutions may not collect any fees other than those stipulated in the fee and refund standard published by the central competent authority pursuant to Paragraph 1 or the fee and refund schedule approved by the local authority pursuant to the preceding paragraph.

Childcare institutions shall enter into a written contract with the legal representative or actual guardian of the child placed in their care that covers the rights and obligations of their childcare services.
The format and contents of the written contract described in the preceding paragraph shall be standardized by the central competent authority in a standard contract form that stipulates the compulsory and prohibited contractual terms.

Childcare institutions shall ensure that the children under their care are covered by group insurance.
In the event of an insured incident during the coverage period described in the preceding paragraph, childcare institutions shall proactively assist in the insurance claims process.
Matters governing the scope, amount, payment and refund method, payment schedule, covered items and standards, rights and obligations, handling methods, and other matters related to the group insurance described in Paragraph 1 shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

To safeguard children’s safety and preserve evidence, childcare institutions shall install surveillance cameras and shall properly manage audio and video recordings, retain recordings for at least 30 days, and keep recordings confidential.
Childcare institutions shall transmit the recorded audio and video described in the preceding paragraph to the internet system established by the local authority for storage. Childcare institutions shall not evade, obstruct, or refuse such transmission.
The central competent authority shall provide subsidies for local authorities to establish the internet system described in the preceding paragraph.
Matters governing installation locations and required functions of the surveillance equipment described in Paragraph 1; allocation of supervisory personnel; audio and video collection, processing, use, and access conditions; inspection/spot-check mechanisms and methods; retention and destruction methods for audio and video recordings; information security measures for the establishment of the internet system described in Paragraph 2, and other related matters shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

Childcare institutions shall formulate and duly implement management plans for the following matters and shall regularly review and improve such plans:
1. Environmental sanitation and food safety.
2. Prevention of diseases, communicable or otherwise
3. Regular safety inspections and maintenance of facilities
4. Safety drills
5. Emergency response measures
6. Other matters related to the management of safety and health

Each childcare institution shall set up a dedicated account for handling the receipt, expenditure, custody, and use of all funds. Legal vouchers shall be obtained for all receipts and expenditures and must be retained for the period of time prescribed by the applicable regulations.
The establishment, acquisition, and custody of account books and vouchers, and other accounting regulations applicable to childcare institutions shall be subject to the relevant tax laws.
Childcare institutions shall operate independently; the finances of a childcare institution affiliated with a legal entity shall be kept strictly separate from those of the legal entity or other institutions affiliated with the legal entity.

Childcare institutionsshall formulate the relevant rescue and care procedures in response to cases of acute illness or accidental injury involving a child, including locations to which the child is to be escorted for medical care, protocols for calling the emergency medical services hotline for support, and measures to be taken before the legal representative or actual guardian arrives.

Childcare institutions shall publicly display the following information:
1. Childcare service recipients and service scope
2. The names, educational backgrounds, or certification of childcare-related personnel
3. The admissions quota approved by the local authority and the actual number of children admitted
4. The management plans formulated in accordance with Article 39
5. The status of group insurance coverage
6. Service fees, refundable items, and amounts
7. Other disclosures required by competent authorities at any level
Childcare institutions shall display prominently information about their childcare personnel arrangements and children admitted for care in a clearly visible location at their premises for parents to review.

Should the legal representative or actual guardian of a child be concerned with the manner or scope of childcare services provided by a childcare institution, they may request an explanation from the institution and may, through mutual agreement, modify or adjust such services as necessary.

The competent authorities at every level shall assist institutional childcare personnel in establishing professional associations at their respective administrative level, assist them in formulating codes of professional ethics, and encourage institutional childcare personnel to organize and participate in labor unions in accordance with the Labor Union Act.
Childcare institutions shall establish a mechanism for institutional childcare personnel to participate in the decision-making process regarding important matters related to childcare services and employee rights and interests.
Chapter IV. Qualifications and Obligations of Personnel and Management of Childcare Services

Family childcare personnel and institutional childcare personnel must be adults who with one of the following:
1. A professional skill certificate as a childcare service provider
2. Graduation from a program, division, department, or graduate institute related to early childhood care, early childhood education, home economics, or nursing at a senior secondary school or higher education institution
Matters related to the qualifications for staff members of family childcare service centers and other childcare institution personnel shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

Supervisory personnel must obtain a certificate of completion for professional training conducted by the local authority and have one of the following qualifications:
1. Having graduated from a master’s (degree) program or above at a college, department, or graduate institute related to early childhood education, early childhood care, home economics, or nursing at a university, and having at least two years of experience in children’s education, care, and caregiving
2. Having graduated from a bachelor’s (degree) program at, or having obtained a minor degree from, a college or department related to early childhood education, early childhood care, home economics, or nursing at a university, and having at least two years of experience in children’s education, care, and caregiving
3. Having graduated with a bachelor’s degree or higher, or having graduated from a college, department, graduate institute, degree program, or division related to early childhood education, early childhood care, home economics, or nursing at a junior college, and having at least three years of experience in children’s education, care, and caregiving.
4. Having graduated from a junior college and having at least four years of experience in children’s education, care, and caregiving
5. Other qualifications set forth by the central competent authority
Experience in children’s education, care, and caregiving, as described in Subparagraphs 1 through 4 of the preceding paragraph, shall refer to service in any of the following positions, supported by a certificate of years of service issued by the local authority or competent education authority:
1. Educare personnel, assistant educare personnel, teachers, educare givers, educare assistants, directors, or principals of nurseries or kindergartens (known collectively as preschools following the system change).
2. Childcare and supervisory personnel at childcare institutions
3. Early intervention educare personnel and assistant educare personnel at early intervention institutions.
4. Childcare personnel at placement and educational facilities

Childcare-related personnel or staff members of a family childcare service center shall not engage in any conduct involving physical or psychological abuse, corporal punishment, bullying, sexual harassment, inappropriate disciplinary measures, or any other form of improper behavior on children, physical, mental, or otherwise.
Conduct described in the preceding paragraph which results in penalties imposed by a local authority under Articles 69 and 76 shall be entered into a penalty database maintained by the central competent authority. The database may be accessed by government agencies (institutions) and authorized institutions, legal entities, or organizations.

Should any childcare-related personnel or staff member of a family childcare service center be found, upon investigation by the local authority, to have engaged in any unlawful conduct pursuant to Paragraph 1 of the preceding article, the competent authority may order the person in question to undertake one or more of the following measures, except where the local authority determines that the person in question should be permanently prohibited from serving as childcare-related personnel or a staff member of a family childcare service center:
1. Attend between three and 12 hours of training in child counseling and discipline, emotional regulation, gender equality education, or other related training
2. Other measures consistent with educational or counseling purposes

Childcare institutions or the competent family childcare service centers shall terminate the contract of any childcare professionals, staff members, or family childcare service center employees found to have engaged in any of the conduct set out in the subparagraphs of this Article. The local authority shall register the offender as being permanently prohibited from serving as childcare-related personnel or as a staff member of a family childcare service center; the local authority shall additionally publish the name of the offender and the affiliated childcare institution:
1. An offense described in Article 2, Subparagraph 1 of the Sexual Assault Crime Prevention Act, with a deferred prosecution disposition or a final and binding conviction
2. An offense described in the Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act, with a deferred prosecution disposition or a final and binding conviction
3. A sexual assault offense, as determined by the local authority following an investigation
4. A serious domestic violence offense, with a final and binding conviction, that is deemed by the local authority as grounds for permanently prohibiting the person from serving as childcare-related personnel or a staff member of a family childcare service center
5. A punishable offense resulting in penalties under the Child and Youth Sexual Exploitation Prevention Act or Article 25 or 27 of the Sexual Harassment Prevention Act that is deemed by the local authority as grounds for permanently prohibiting the person from serving as childcarerelated personnel or a staff member of a family childcare service center
6. A punishable offense resulting in penalties issued by the competent authority at any level under Article 97 of the Child and Juvenile Welfare and Rights Protection Act that is deemed by the local authority as grounds for permanently prohibiting the person from serving as childcare-related personnel or a staff member of a family childcare service center
7. Failure to report a (suspected) sexual assault incident, in accordance with Article 59, Paragraph 1 herein, at the childcare institution where the childcare professional, staff member, or family childcare service center employee served, thereby resulting in repeated sexual assault incidents within the institution; or falsification, alteration, destruction, or concealment of evidence of a sexual assault incident committed by another person within the childcare institution, as verified by the local authority
8. Falsification, alteration, destruction, or concealment of evidence of a narcotics hazard offense committed by another person within the childcare institution, as verified by the local authority
9. An offense leading to penalties under Article 69 herein that is deemed by the local authority as grounds for permanently prohibiting the person from serving as childcare-related personnel or a staff member of a family childcare service center
10. A violation of the applicable laws or regulations, creating a risk of harm to children, as verified by the local authority, which determines the offense to be grounds for permanently prohibiting the person from serving as childcare-related personnel or a staff member of a family childcare service center

Childcare institutions or entities commissioned to operate family childcare service centers shall terminate the contract of any childcare professionals, staff members, or staff members of a family childcare service center found to have engaged in any of the following conduct; the local authority shall publish the name of the offender and the name of the childcare institution:
1. A punishable offense resulting in penalties under the Child and Youth Sexual Exploitation Prevention Act, Article 25 or 27 of the Sexual Harassment Prevention Act, or Article 38-2, Paragraph 1 of the Gender Equality in Employment Act that is deemed by the competent authority as grounds for prohibiting the person from serving as childcare-related personnel or as a staff member of a family childcare service center
2. An offense under Article 25–1, Paragraph 1 of the Animal Protection Act with a final and binding conviction issued within the most recent five-year period
3. A domestic violence offense with a deferred prosecution disposition or a final and binding conviction issued within the most recent five-year period
4. An offense resulting in penalties from the competent authority at any level pursuant to Article 97 of the Child and Juvenile Welfare and Rights Protection Act that is deemed by the local authority to be grounds for prohibiting the person from serving as childcare-related personnel or as a staff member of a family childcare service center
5. An offense resulting in penalties under Article 69 herein from a local authority that deems the offense as grounds for prohibiting the person from serving as childcare-related personnel or as a staff member of a family childcare service center
6. Violation of applicable laws or regulations in such a manner that poses danger to children, as verified by the local authority, which deems the violation as grounds for prohibiting the person from serving as childcare-related personnel or as a staff member of a family childcare service center
A person meeting the description of Subparagraph 2 or 3 of the preceding paragraph shall be prohibited from serving as childcare-related personnel or as a staff member of a family childcare service center for a period of five years, counting from the date on which the conviction or disposition becomes final. A person meeting the description of Subparagraph 1 or Subparagraphs 4 through 6 of the preceding paragraph shall be prohibited from serving as childcare-related personnel or as a staff member of a family childcare service center for a period of one to four years, as determined by the local authority based on the severity of the offense.

Persons under any of the following circumstances shall be prohibited from serving as childcare-related personnel or as staff members of family childcare service centers:
1. Any circumstances described in the subparagraphs of Article 49 herein
2. Any circumstances described under Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 2 or 3 in the most recent five years, or under Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 1 or Subparagraphs 4 through 6 of the same article within the most recent one to four years, as determined under Paragraph 2 of the same article
3. Any circumstances described in the subparagraphs of Article 23 of the Early Childhood Education and Care Act
4. Any circumstances described in the subparagraphs of Article 24 of the Early Childhood Education and Care Act within the most recent one to four years, as determined by the same act
5. Any circumstances described in Article 12, Subparagraphs 3 to 12 of the Preschool Educators’ Act
6. Any circumstances described in the subparagraphs of Article 13 of the Preschool Educators’ Act within the most recent one to four years, as determined by the same act
7. Any circumstances described in Article 14, Paragraph 1, Subparagraphs 3 through 11 of the Teachers’ Act
8. Any circumstances described in Article 15, Paragraph 1 of the Teachers’ Act in the most recent one to four years
9. Any circumstances described in Article 18, Paragraph 1 of the Teachers’ Act resulting in a suspension of between six months and three years
10. Any circumstance described in Article 29, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 1 or the first half of Paragraph 3 of the Gender Equity Education Act
11. Any circumstance described in Article 29, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 2 or the proviso of Paragraph 3 of the Gender Equity Education Act in the most recent one to four years
12. Any circumstance specified in Article 9, Paragraph 6, Subparagraph 1 or 2 of the Supplementary and Continuing Education Act
13. Any circumstances specified in Article 9, Paragraph 6, Subparagraph 3 of the Supplementary and Continuing Education Act in the most recent one to four years
A person may not be employed as childcare service personnel if they fall under any of the subparagraphs of the preceding paragraph and have been reported on record pursuant to the regulations prescribed under Article 27, Paragraph 4 of the Early Childhood Education and Care Act; Article 16, Paragraph 4 of the Preschool Educators’ Act; Article 20, Paragraph 4 of the Teachers’ Act; Article 30, Paragraph 4 of the Gender Equity Education Act; or Article 9, Paragraph 12 of the Supplementary and Continuing Education Act (collectively, “reporting requirements”). Childcare institutions or the entity commissioned to operate family childcare service centers shall terminate the contract of any such persons already employed. A person who has been reported on record in accordance with regulations other than the aforementioned reporting requirements may not be employed; any such person already employed shall have their contract terminated pursuant to Article 49, to Paragraph 1 of the preceding article, or to the preceding paragraph.

The local authority shall determine whether, under any of the following circumstances, a childcare institution’s responsible person should be permanently prohibited from serving as a responsible person and whether their name shall be published:
1. Any circumstances described under the subparagraphs of Article 49 herein
2. Commission of any of the following offenses and conviction in a final and binding judgment:
 1) Offenses of corruption under the Anti-Corruption Act
 2) Intentional homicide, intentional serious injury, robbery, extortion, threats to obtain property, or kidnapping for ransom
 3) Offenses under Article 7 or 8 of the Firearms, Ammunition and Knives Control Act
 4) Offenses under Article 3, 4, or 6 of the Organized Crime Prevention Act.

The local authority shall determine whether, under any of the circumstances described in Article 50, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 1 or Subparagraph 4 through 6, a childcare institution’s responsible person shall be prohibited from serving as a responsible person for a period of one to four years and whether their name shall be published.

A person who, based on objective facts, is considered likely to cause harm to children and is determined by the local authority to be unfit for employment shall not serve as childcare-related personnel.
Once the cause described in the preceding paragraph ceases to exist, the person may, upon determination by the local authority, be permitted to serve as childcare-related personnel in accordance with this Act.
The determination under Paragraph 1 shall be made by a review panel assembled by the local authority composed of physicians in a related discipline, child welfare specialists, and other relevant scholars and experts.

Family childcare personnel shall be limited to providing childcare services in the child’s home if a person cohabiting with them falls under any of the following circumstances:
1. Any circumstances described in the subparagraphs of Article 49 herein
2. Any circumstances described in the subparagraphs of Article 50, Paragraph 1 herein
3. Any circumstances determined by the local authority, based on objective facts, to pose a risk of harm to children
The determination of Subparagraph 3 of the preceding paragraph shall be made by a review panel assembled by the local authority composed of physicians in a related discipline, child welfare specialists, and other relevant scholars and experts.

The local authority shall revoke the establishment permit of a childcare institution whose responsible person falls under any of the circumstances set out in Article 47, Paragraph 1; Article 52; or Article 53, except as otherwise provided in Paragraph 2 herein.
If the responsible person of a childcare institution commissioned by a government agency (institution) or public school falls under any of the circumstances set out in Article 47, Paragraph 1; Article 52; or Article 53, the local authority shall order the replacement of the responsible person within a specified time frame.
During the investigation period, if a staff member of a family childcare service center or the responsible person, supervisory personnel, institutional childcare personnel, or a staff member of a childcare institution is suspected under any of the circumstances set out in Article 47, Paragraph 1; Article 49; Article 50; or Article 51, Paragraph 1, the local authority shall order the childcare institution or entity commissioned to operate the family childcare service center to temporarily suspend or adjust the duties of the person concerned. If, following investigation, it is determined that none of the circumstances described in the cited articles apply, any salary withheld during the suspension period shall be retroactively paid.
The local authority shall order family childcare personnel falling under any of the circumstances set out in Article 47, Paragraph 1; Article 49; Article 50; or Article 51, Paragraph 1 to cease services and shall immediately transfer the children under their care. Registrations already submitted by such persons under Article 13, Paragraph 1 shall be revoked.

Upon receipt of a complaint or becoming aware that childcare-related personnel, persons cohabiting with family childcare personnel, or staff members of a family childcare service center are suspected of committing any unlawful act under Article 47, Paragraph 1; Article 49; Article 50; Article 51, Paragraph 1; Article 52; Article 53; Article 54, Paragraph 1; or Article 55, the local authority shall take action within two working days.
Upon acceptance of a suspected violation report, as described in the preceding paragraph, the local authority shall appoint dedicated personnel or form an investigation panel to conduct an investigation. The investigation shall be completed within 30 days of the panel’s establishment; however, the 30-day limit may be extended once for up to 30 additional days where necessary. The parties concerned, the whistleblower, and the family childcare service center or childcare institution shall be notified.
The local authority shall establish a review panel to review the investigation results from the preceding paragraph. Where necessary, the review panel may invite scholars/experts, physicians, medical personnel, or gender equality experts to provide professional opinions.
The review panel shall include representatives from the competent authority, experts in early childhood care and child welfare, legal experts, representatives of childcare services organizations, representatives of childcare professionals, representatives of parental associations, and scholars and experts in relevant fields.
The regulations governing the investigation procedures, qualifications of dedicated personnel, composition and qualifications of the review panel, number of members, and other related matters under Paragraphs 2 through 4 of this article shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

The local authority shall notify the offender and the legal representative or actual guardian of the child involved in the incident under review in accordance with Paragraph 3 of the preceding article in writing within 15 days. The notification shall state the facts and reasons supporting the decision.
The legal representative or actual guardian of the child or the offender may file an administrative appeal in accordance with law if they are dissatisfied with the decision of the review panel concerning a violation of Article 47, Paragraph 1 of the preceding paragraph.
The central competent authority shall release a summary of the decision made by the review panel described in Paragraph 1.

Childcare-related personnel or staff members of a family childcare service center who, in the course of performing their duties, become aware of any unlawful incident under Article 57, Paragraph 1 shall report such incident to the local authority within 24 hours.
The identity of the whistleblower described in the preceding paragraph shall be kept confidential.
Childcare institutions or entities commissioned to operate family childcare service centers shall not dismiss, demote, reduce the salary of, take adverse action against, or otherwise infringe upon any legal, contractual, or customary rights or interests of personnel who make a report under Paragraph 1.

For childcare-related personnel or staff members of a family childcare service center who fall under any circumstance set out in Article 57, Paragraph 1, the local authority shall handle the reporting of, the inquiry into, and the collection, processing, and use of information in accordance with the applicable regulations.
When a childcare institution applies for an establishment permit, the local authority shall inquire whether the responsible person falls under Article 49; Article 50; Article 51, Paragraph 1; Article 52; or Article 53. The same shall apply when an institution requests a change of responsible person.
Before employing supervisory personnel, institutional childcare personnel, or staff members, childcare institutions shall inquire as to whether such persons fall under Article 49, Article 50, or Article 51, Paragraph 1. The same inquiry shall be conducted by entities commissioned to operate family childcare service centers before employing staff members. Regular inquiries shall be conducted for persons already employed.
Before employing supervisory personnel, institutional childcare personnel, or staff members, childcare institutions shall submit a roster of prospective hires and a copy of qualification documents, affidavits, health examination results, police criminal records (issued within the most recent three-month period), and other supporting documents required by the central competent authority to the local authority for approval. The same shall apply to entities commissioned to operate family childcare service centers prior to hiring staff members. Changes involving such personnel other than new hires shall be reported for recordation within 14 days to the local authority, which shall proactively verify the documents submitted and may assign personnel to conduct inspections.
The local authority may, for inquiries made pursuant to Paragraph 2 or Paragraph 3, use databases established under the Child and Juvenile Welfare and Rights Protection Act, the Early Childhood Education and Care Act, the Preschool Educators’ Act, the Teachers’ Act, the Supplementary and Continuing Education Act, and the Gender Equity Education Act.
The regulations governing reporting; the collection, inquiry, processing, and use of information before and during employment; and other related matters under the preceding five paragraphs shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

After becoming aware that childcare-related personnel of a childcare institution, family childcare personnel, or persons cohabiting with family childcare personnel are suspected of involvement in an unlawful act under Article 57, Paragraph 1, the local authority shall immediately notify the legal representative or actual guardian of the child placed in care. During the administrative investigation, criminal investigation, or court proceedings, the local authority shall assist the childcare institution and family childcare personnel in finding temporary placement for the child in accordance with the wishes of their legal representative or actual guardian and shall strengthen visitation and supervision. When necessary, the local authority may mandate the suspension of new admissions or the suspension of childcare services.
If a person cohabiting with family childcare personnel is suspected of violating Article 57, Paragraph 1, the local authority may, during the administrative investigation, criminal investigation, or court proceedings, restrict the family childcare personnel to provide childcare services only in the child’s home.

Childcare professionals or staff members shall not lease or lend their childcare service certificates or qualification certificates to others.
A childcare institution shall not lease or borrow the qualification certificate of any childcare professional who does not serve in the institution.

Childcare professionals shall complete at least 18 hours of professional competency training each year. Such training shall include at least one gender equality course every other year.
Childcare professionals shall complete at least eight hours of emergency pediatric basic life support training within two years before they begin providing childcare services or within three months after beginning service, and shall further complete at least eight hours of pediatric basic life support training, at least three hours of accident injury prevention and response training, and at least one emergency care drill every two years.
The local authority shall, either directly or by commissioning a relevant agency, institution, organization, or professional society or association to do so, organize the training, courses, and drills described in the preceding paragraph at least once every quarter. Childcare institutions and family childcare service centers shall provide the necessary assistance.
Regulations governing the providers and instructors for and the method for crediting hours earned for the completion of the professional competency training described in Paragraph 1; the items and implementation methods for the pediatric basic life support training, accident injury prevention and response training, and emergency response drills described in the preceding two paragraphs; and other related matters shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

Family childcare personnel and childcare institutions shall assist the competent local health authorities in organizing child development screenings and health promotion campaigns.
Family childcare personnel, staff members of family childcare service centers, and childcare institutions that suspect a child admitted for care of having a developmental delay shall report the matter to the local authority. Family childcare personnel shall also notify the competent family childcare service center when making such reports.
The local authority shall document reports filed under the preceding paragraph for children suspected of having a developmental delay and shall provide, or refer them to, appropriate services as necessary. The local authority may also seek assistance from family childcare personnel, family childcare service centers, or childcare institutions.

Childcare-related personnel shall keep confidential all information concerning children and their legal representatives or actual guardians except with the consent of a legal representative or actual guardian or where otherwise required by law.

The legal representative or actual guardian of a child shall pay childcare-related fees and provide vaccination records in accordance with the written childcare contract. If the child has a special physical or mental health condition, they shall inform the family childcare personnel or childcare institution and, when necessary, provide the relevant health records.
The legal representative or actual guardian of a child shall, to the extent possible, participate in parenting activities organized by the childcare institution, or in case studies and activities pertaining to the child’s special needs during care.
The competent authorities at all levels shall proactively provide resources and assistance to the legal representative or actual guardian described in the preceding paragraph.

The legal representative or actual guardian of a child who believes that a care dispute arising from the family childcare personnel’s childcare services has harmed the child’s rights and interests may apply to the family childcare service center for mediation. If mediation by the family childcare service center is unsuccessful, the legal representative or actual guardian of the child may, within 30 days from the day after receiving the mediation result, apply to the local authority where the center is located for a second mediation.
The legal representative or actual guardian of a child who believes that a care dispute arising from a childcare institution’s childcare services has harmed the child’s rights and interests may file an objection with the childcare institution. If dissatisfied with the childcare institution’s decisions, the legal representative or actual guardian of the child may, within 30 days from the day after becoming aware of such decisions, apply to the local authority where the childcare institution is located for mediation.
The local authority may conduct the necessary investigations upon receiving an application for mediation under the preceding two paragraphs.
Mediation for the same underlying facts shall, in principle, be conducted once only.
The local authority shall notify the applicant in writing of the results of the second mediation under Paragraph 1 or the mediation results under Paragraph 2. The notification shall state the facts and reasons supporting the decision.
If, during mediation, objection handling, or investigation, the family childcare service center, childcare institution, or local authority becomes aware of an Article 57 violation committed by any childcare-related personnel, it shall immediately suspend the relevant procedures and handle the matter in accordance with this Act.
If, during mediation under Paragraph 1 or objection handling under Paragraph 2, the family childcare service center or childcare institution becomes aware of a suspected unlawful act, it shall report the matter in accordance with Article 59 herein or other applicable laws and regulations.

When the local authority or an institution, organization, or professional commissioned by the local authority conducts visits, inspections, or investigations or provides supervision or subsidies related to childcare services, all childcare-related personnel, childcare institutions, children’s legal representatives or actual guardians, and other relevant persons shall cooperate and provide relevant information. The local authority may request additional information and assistance from the relevant police, household registration, financial, and education agencies, institutions, organizations, or legal entities, which shall have a duty to cooperate.
The local authority shall exercise the due care of a prudent administrator, conduct information security audits, and comply with the Personal Data Protection Act in retaining, processing, and using information obtained under the preceding paragraph.
Chapter V. Penalties

Should any childcare-related personnel or staff members of a family childcare service center violate Article 47, Paragraph 1 herein and commit any of the following acts against a child, the offender shall be fined no less than NT$60,000 and no more than NT$600,000, and their name and the name of their affiliated childcare institution shall be published:
1. Physical or psychological abuse
2. Severe corporal punishment, bullying, sexual harassment, inappropriate disciplinary measures, or other acts of physical or psychological violence or improper behavior

A person who establishes a childcare institution and admits children for care without obtaining the required permit, thus violating Article 26, Paragraph 2; Article 27, Paragraph 3; or Article 28, Paragraph 5 herein, shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$60,000 and no more than NT$300,000 and shall be ordered to stop admitting children; refusal to comply shall be subject to repeat penalties.
In the circumstances described in the preceding paragraph, the local authority shall publish the address of the premises and the name of the offender and shall notify the legal representatives or actual guardians of admitted children.
In the circumstances described in Paragraph 1, the local authority shall order the offender to transfer the children under their care within one month; where transfer is difficult, the local authority shall provide assistance.
Failure to comply with the transfer order under the preceding paragraph shall result in a fine of no less than NT$60,000 and no more than NT$300,000, and the transfer order shall be enforced by the local authority.

Family childcare personnel falling under any of the following circumstances shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$60,000 and no more than NT$300,000, and such personnel shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties. For serious offenses or where the person fails to make improvements after three penalties, their registration shall be revoked:
1. Violation of the regulations concerning the number of children admitted for care under Article 13, Paragraph 5 herein, where five or more children are admitted
2. Violation of Article 55, Paragraph 1 herein by providing services beyond the scope of permissible childcare services in the child’s home
3. Failure to comply with an order issued by the local authority under Article 56, Paragraph 4 herein to cease services and immediately transfer the children under their care
4. Failure to comply with an order issued by the local authority under Article 61, Paragraph 1 herein to suspend new admissions or suspend childcare services
5. Failure to comply with an order issued by the local authority under Article 61, Paragraph 2 herein by providing services beyond the scope of permissible childcare services in the child’s home

The responsible person of a childcare institution falling under any of the following circumstances shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$60,000 and no more than NT$300,000, and the institution shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties. For serious offenses or where the institution fails to make improvements after three penalties, it may, depending on the severity of the case, be ordered to suspend admissions for a period of six months to one year, suspend operations for a period of one to three years, or have its establishment permit revoked:
1. Violation of the provisions on the number of children admitted for care under Article 27, Paragraph 4 or Article 28, Paragraph 6
2. Allowing the presence of persons described in Article 34, Paragraph 3, Subparagraph 2
3. Violation of Article 34, Paragraph 4 herein by evading, obstructing, or refusing oversight, inspection, or evaluation by the local authority, or by concealing children during inspections
4. Failure to make improvements after follow-up evaluation and supervision under Article 34, Paragraph 5 herein
5. Failure to report fee and refund standards to the local authority for approval under Article 35, Paragraph 2 herein
6. Violation of Article 35, Paragraph 3 herein by charging fees other than the fee and refund items and for purposes permitted by the central competent authority or in excess of amounts approved by the local authority
7. Employing childcare professionals or staff members who fall under any circumstance set out in Article 49; Article 50, Paragraph 1; or Article 51, Paragraph 1 herein, or failing to terminate the contract upon becoming aware of such circumstances
8. Failure to comply with an order issued by the local authority under Article 56, Paragraph 2 herein to replace the responsible person
9. Failure to comply with an order issued by the local authority under Article 56, Paragraph 3 herein to suspend or adjust the duties of childcare-related personnel
10. Violation of Article 61, Paragraph 1 herein due to failure to comply with an order of the local authority to suspend new admissions or suspend childcare services.
11. Violation of Article 62, Paragraph 2 by leasing or lending the qualification certificate of a childcare professional who does not serve in the institution.
An entity commissioned to operate family childcare service centers falling under any of the following circumstances shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$60,000 and no more than NT$300,000, and the entity shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties:
1. Employing staff members who fall under any circumstance set out in Article 49, Article 50, or Article 51, Paragraph 1 herein, or failing to terminate the contract upon becoming aware of such circumstances
2. Failure to comply with Article 56, Paragraph 3 by not following an order of the local authority to suspend or adjust the duties of staff members of the family childcare service center

The responsible person of a childcare institution falling under any of the following circumstances shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$30,000 and no more than NT$300,000, and the institution shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties. For serious offenses or where the institution fails to make improvements, the institution may, depending on the severity of the case, be ordered to suspend admissions for a period of six months to one year, suspend operations for a period of one to three years, or have its establishment permit revoked:
1. Violation of Article 27, Paragraph 4 or Article 28, Paragraph 6 herein regarding qualifications and allocation of childcare-related personnel or the ratio of childcare personnel to children admitted for care
2. Failure to obtain group insurance coverage for children as required under Article 37, Paragraph 1 herein
3. Failure to properly manage audio and video recordings and retain them for at least 30 days as required under Article 38, Paragraph 1 herein, or failure to provide such recordings in accordance with the access conditions and procedures prescribed under Paragraph 4 of the same article
4. Violation of Article 38, Paragraph 2 by evading, obstructing, or refusing to transmit audio and video recordings to the internet system established by the local authority
5. Failure to obtain approval from the local authority prior to employing supervisory personnel, institutional childcare personnel, or staff members as required under Article 60, Paragraph 4 herein
An entity commissioned to operate a family childcare service center that fails to obtain approval from the local authority prior to employing staff members, as required under Article 60, Paragraph 4 herein, shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$30,000 and no more than NT$300,000, and the entity shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties.

Where any of the following circumstances occurs, a fine of no less than NT$30,000 and no more than NT$150,000 shall be imposed on the childcare-related personnel, who shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties:
1. Childcare-related personnel of a childcare institution fail to maintain the confidentiality of audio and video recordings as required under Article 38, Paragraph 1 herein.
2. Childcare professionals or staff members violate Article 62, Paragraph 1 herein by leasing or lending their childcare service certificates or qualification certificates to others.
3. Childcare-related personnel fail to maintain the confidentiality of information concerning children, their legal representatives, or actual guardians as required under Article 65 herein.
Where supervisory personnel, institutional childcare personnel, or staff members of a childcare institution commit any of the acts described in Subparagraph 1 or Subparagraph 3 of the preceding paragraph, the responsible person shall be subject to an additional fine of no less than NT$30,000 and no more than NT$150,000. However, no penalty shall be imposed on the responsible person if they voluntarily report the matter before it becomes known to the local authority.

A person who does not possess the qualifications of family childcare personnel and violates Article 13, Paragraph 1 herein by providing family childcare services shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$20,000 and no more than NT$100,000 and shall be ordered to cease admissions and immediately transfer the children under their care. The offender’s name may also be published.
A person who possesses the qualifications of family childcare personnel but provides family childcare services without completing registration under Article 13, Paragraph 1 herein, or who provides such services during a suspension of admissions under Article 13, Paragraph 2 herein, shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$10,000 and no more than NT$50,000 and shall be ordered to complete registration by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in a fine of no less than NT$20,000 and no more than NT$100,000 and an order to transfer the children under their care within one month. The name of the offender may also be published.
In circumstances described in the preceding two paragraphs, the local authority shall immediately notify the legal representative or actual guardian of the affected children and shall assist in the transfer process by strengthening visitation and supervision.
A person who refuses to comply with a transfer order under Paragraph 1 or Paragraph 2 herein shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$20,000 and no more than NT$100,000, and the local authority shall enforce the transfer order for the children under their care.
Until registration is completed pursuant to Paragraph 2 herein, family childcare personnel shall not increase the number of children under their care. Violators of this provision shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$20,000 and no more than NT$100,000 per violation, and the local authority shall enforce the transfer order for any additional children admitted.
