Should childcare-related personnel or staff members of a family childcare service center engage in conduct specified in Article 47, Paragraph 1, including corporal punishment, bullying, sexual harassment, inappropriate disciplinary measures, or other physical or psychological violence or improper behavior on children, and the circumstances are not serious, a fine of no less than NT$6,000 and no more than NT$60,000 shall be imposed on the offender, and the offender’s name and the name of the childcare institution to which they belong shall be published. However, if the responsible person voluntarily reports the matter before it becomes known to the local authority, the name of the institution may be excluded. Minor offenses may be handled in accordance with Article 48 herein.

Should childcare-related personnel fail to comply with orders from the local authority under the main clause of Article 48 herein without justifiable cause, a fine of no less than NT$10,000 and no more than NT$50,000 shall be imposed, and such childcare-related personnel shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties.

Family childcare personnel falling under any of the following circumstances shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$10,000 and no more than NT$50,000, and such family childcare personnel shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties. For serious offenses or where the family childcare personnel fails to make improvements after three penalties, the name of such family childcare personnel may be published and their registration may be revoked:
1. Evasion, obstruction, or refusal of oversight by the local competent authority and the family childcare service center under Article 13, Paragraph 4 herein, or concealing children during inspections
2. Violation of the regulations on the number of children admitted for care under Article 13, Paragraph 5 herein
3. Violating Article 16 herein by charging fees other than the fee and refund items or standards permitted by the local authority
4. Failure to enter into a written contract with the legal representative or actual guardian of a child, as required under Article 17, Paragraph 1 herein
5. Failure to obtain professional liability insurance coverage prior to admitting children, as required under Article 18, Paragraph 1 herein
6. Failure to provide dedicated childcare services during service hours and at the designated service premises, as required under Article 19 herein
7. Failure to report an incident to the local authority under Article 59, Paragraph 1 herein
A person whose registration is revoked under the preceding paragraph shall be ineligible to register as family childcare personnel for a period of one year from the date of revocation.

Any person other than family childcare personnel who violates Article 13, Paragraph 4 herein by evading, obstructing, or refusing inspection by the local competent authority and the family childcare service center of the registered childcare service location, or by concealing children during such inspections, shall be fined no less than NT$10,000 and no more than NT$50,000.

The responsible person of a childcare institution falling under any of the following circumstances shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$10,000 and no more than NT$50,000, and the institution shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeat penalties. For serious offenses or where the institution fails to make improvements after three penalties, the institution may, depending on the severity of the case, be ordered to suspend admissions for a period six months to one year, suspend operations for a period one to three years, or have its establishment permit revoked:
1. Violation of the regulations prescribed in Article 27, Paragraph 4 or Article 28, Paragraph 6 regarding the area, facilities and equipment, expansion, relocation, suspension, closure, or resumption of operations of a childcare institution
2. Admitting children aged over two years in circumstances not permitted under Article 29, or violating the time limit for the admission of such children under the same Article
3. Failure to enter into a written contract with the legal representative or actual guardian of a child, as required under Article 36, Paragraph 1
4. Unlawful acts, as described in Article 47, Paragraph 1, by childcare-related personnel under the institution (with no penalty imposed on the responsible person if they voluntarily report the matter before it becomes known to the local authority)
5. Failure to report an incident to the local authority by childcare-related personnel under the institution, as required under Article 59, Paragraph 1
6. Violation of Article 59, Paragraph 3 by imposing dismissal, demotion, salary reduction, or other adverse measures against personnel who have made a report under Paragraph 1 of the same Article
7. Failure to conduct required inquiries prior to employing supervisory personnel, institutional childcare personnel, or staff members, or failure to conduct regular reviews after employment, as required under Article 60, Paragraph 3
8. Violation of Article 60, Paragraph 4 by failing to report changes other than new hires to the local authority for recordation within 14 days
An entity commissioned to operate family childcare service centers falling under any of the following circumstances shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$10,000 and no more than NT$50,000, and the entity shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeated penalties:
1. Failure to report an incident to the local authority by staff members of the family childcare service center, as required under Article 59, Paragraph 1
2. Failure to conduct required inquiries prior to employing staff members, or failure to conduct regular inquiries after employment, as required under Article 60, Paragraph 3
3. Violation of Article 60, Paragraph 4 by failing to report changes other than new hires to the local competent authority for recordation within 14 days

Family childcare personnel violating the supervision or management provisions prescribed under Article 13, Paragraph 5 and subsequently failing to rectify the situation by a given deadline after being ordered to do so shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$6,000 and no more than NT$30,000. Repeat penalties may be imposed. For serious offenses or where such family childcare personnel fail to make improvements after three penalties, their registration shall be revoked.
A person whose registration is revoked under the preceding paragraph shall be ineligible to register as family childcare personnel for a period of one year, counting from the date of revocation.

The responsible person of a childcare institution falling under any of the following circumstances shall be subject to a fine of no less than NT$6,000 and no more than NT$30,000, and the institution shall be ordered to rectify the situation by a given deadline. Failure to comply shall result in repeated penalties. For serious offenses or where the institution fails to make improvements after three penalties, the responsible person of the childcare institution may, depending on the severity of the case, be ordered to suspend admissions for a period six months to one year, suspend operations for a period one to three years, or have its establishment permit revoked:
1. Failure to assist in handling group insurance claims, as required under Article 37, Paragraph 2
2. Violation of Article 38, Paragraph 4 regarding the installation areas and required functions of surveillance cameras or staffing of monitoring personnel
3. Failure to establish, properly implement, or regularly review and improve the management plan, as required under Article 39
4. Failure to establish dedicated accounts, obtain lawful income and expense vouchers, or retain such documents for the mandated period, as required under Article 40, Paragraph 1
5. Failure to establish an acute illness or accident injury response mechanism for children, as required under Article 41
6. Failure to disclose information required under Article 42, Paragraph 1

Where a childcare institution, in stipulating the content of a written contract, violates the standard contract form and the required and prohibited clauses prescribed by the central competent authority under Article 36, Paragraph 2, the institution shall be ordered by the local competent authority to amend the contract within a specified time limit. Failure to comply shall result in a fine of no less than NT$30,000 and no more than NT$300,000; where a further order to amend the contract is issued and the institution again fails to comply by the deadline, a fine of no less than NT$50,000 and no more than NT$500,000 shall be imposed for each missed deadline.
Where family childcare personnel, in stipulating the content of a written contract, violate the standard contract form and the required and prohibited clauses prescribed by the central competent authority under Article 17, Paragraph 2, the personnel shall be ordered by the local competent authority to amend the contract within a specified time limit. Failure to comply shall result in a fine of no less than NT$6,000 and no more than NT$30,000 for each missed deadline.

Should any of the following circumstances occur, the offender concerned shall be ordered to rectify the situation within a specified time limit. Failure to comply shall result in a fine of no less than NT$6,000 and no more than NT$30,000 for each violation:
1. Violation of the implementation standards set forth in accordance with Article 9, Paragraph 2
2. Failure of family childcare personnel to deliver a copy of the written contract to the family childcare service center, as required under the latter part of Article 17, Paragraph 1
3. Admission by a childcare institution of children other than those permitted without approval from the local authority, as required under Article 26, Paragraph 4
4. Failure of a childcare institution to disclose information on its childcare personnel and the children under its care, as required under Article 42, Paragraph 2
5. Failure of childcare professionals to complete at least 18 hours of childcare professional competency training per year, as required under the first half of Article 63, Paragraph 1
6. Failure of childcare professionals to complete at least eight hours of pediatric basic life support training within two years prior to or within three months after commencing service, as required under the first half of Article 63, Paragraph 2
7. Failure of childcare professionals to complete, within every two-year period, an additional eight hours of pediatric basic life support training, three hours of accident injury prevention and response training, and at least one emergency care drill, as required under the proviso of Article 63, Paragraph 2
No penalty shall be imposed where any circumstance under Subparagraph 1 or Subparagraphs 5 through 7 of the preceding paragraph is not attributable to the childcare professional, or where any circumstance under Subparagraph 3 or 4 is not attributable to the childcare institution, as determined by the local authority.
Where any circumstance under the preceding paragraph is attributable to a childcare institution, the institution shall be ordered to rectify the situation within a specified time limit. Failure to make rectification by the deadline shall result in a fine of no less than NT$6,000 and no more than NT$30,000 imposed on the responsible person for each missed deadline. For serious offenses or where the childcare institution fails to make improvements after three penalties, the childcare institution may, depending on the severity of the case, be ordered to suspend admissions for a period of six months to one year, suspend operations for a period of one to three years, or have its establishment permit revoked.

Childcare-related personnel, childcare institutions, legal representatives or actual guardians of children, and other relevant persons, organizations, or legal entities who, without justifiable cause, violate Article 68, Paragraph 1 shall be fined no less than NT$6,000 and no more than NT$30,000 for each offense.

Family childcare personnel who are in violation of this Act may be issued demerit points based on the severity of threat posed to childcare quality and child safety, in addition to any applicable penalties, improvement orders, and other necessary measures.
No demerit points shall be recorded for persons whose registration has already been revoked.
Family childcare personnel accumulating a specified number of demerit points within any rolling two-year period shall be subject to suspension of new admissions for a specified period o time by the competent authority, which shall assist in transferring children in accordance with the parents’ wishes. Family childcare personnel ordered to suspend new admissions twice within any rolling five-year period shall have their registration revoked.
A person whose registration is revoked under the preceding paragraph shall be ineligible to register as family childcare personnel for a period of one year from the date of revocation.
Regulations governing the applicable provisions, the number of demerit points, the duration of suspension of new admissions, notification procedures, conditions for registration revocation, and other related matters under the preceding four paragraphs shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.

Orders to rectify a situation by a given deadline and the imposition of penalties under this Act shall be carried out by the local authority.
Should a childcare institution be subject to a fine, prohibition on admissions, suspension of operations, or revocation of its establishment permit imposed by the local competent authority under this Act, the name of the institution and the name of its responsible person shall be published, unless otherwise provided herein.
The duration of publication of the name of the offender, the name of the childcare institution, the name of the responsible person, and the address of the premises shall be prescribed by the central competent authority.
If a childcare institution is a legal entity and its establishment permit is revoked by the local authority, the local authority shall notify a court of law to process the dissolution registration.
Chapter VI. Supplementary Provisions

Family childcare personnel who, prior to the implementation of this Act, have completed professional training courses for childcare personnel, obtained a certificate of completion, and been issued a family childcare service certificate may, after the implementation of this Act, continue to provide family childcare services in accordance with the provisions herein.
Persons who, prior to the implementation of this Act, have completed professional training courses for childcare personnel and obtained a certificate of completion but have not yet obtained a family childcare service certificate may, within one year from the date of implementation of this Act, apply to the local competent authority for registration of family childcare services pursuant to Article 13, Paragraph 1 herein and, upon obtaining a family childcare service certificate, provide family childcare services in accordance with this Act.

A person who, prior to the implementation of this Act, has served as supervisory personnel and meets any of the following qualifications may continue to serve as supervisory personnel:
1. Having graduated from a master’s (degree) program (or above) at a college, department, or graduate institute related to early childhood education, early childhood care, home economics, or nursing with two or more years of experience in children’s education, care, and caregiving
2. Having passed the senior civil service examination or an equivalent civil service examination in social administration or social work with two or more years of work experience at a competent social welfare authority or social welfare institution

Fees shall be waived for the issuance of a family childcare service certificate under Article 13, Paragraph 1 herein, as well as for the issuance of a childcare institution permit under Article 26, Paragraph 2; Article 27, Paragraph 3; or Article 28, Paragraph 5 herein.
Local authority personnel shall present identification documents or wear recognizable badges when conducting supervision, oversight, inspections, or evaluations of childcare services.

Beginning on the date of implementation of this Act, the management of family childcare and childcare institutions shall be governed by the provisions of this Act. Provisions of the Child and Juvenile Welfare and Rights Protection Act concerning family childcare services and nursery service centers shall no longer apply.
The enforcement rules for this Act shall be formulated by the central competent authority.
The date of implementation of this Act shall be set by the Executive Yuan.
